tool_args.rationale: The five paid rows show positive short-window gain but do not constrain the slow adaptation behavior at the target horizon. The slow-horizon discriminating probe is the least costly relevant way to calibrate the reversal before fitting and confirming a model.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit four-parameter dual-exponential reversal from the five short-horizon rows
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All observations have H≤0.48, so they poorly identify the slow timescale/amplitude and cannot establish the forecast behavior near H=19.9.
More short-horizon samples would not resolve the key long-horizon ambiguity as directly.
Irrelevant to the stated target law and expressly not worth its cost.
The supplied data have s_grad=0 throughout, leaving its sink-coupling parameter unidentifiable; the targeted probe is the recommended first measurement.
